(CoinDesk) Summary * Gemini replaced Zebra with Zakura to run its Zcash systems, cutting the time needed to catch up with the network from nearly a day to just over six hours. * The switch comes before Zcash’s planned NU7 upgrade, which would reduce block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds and require network computers to process transactions three times as often. * Developers are targeting Nov. 5 for the mainnet upgrade, though Gemini has not published tests showing how Zakura performs under the faster schedule. Crypto exchange Gemini (GEMI) has switched the software running its Zcash systems ahead of a planned upgrade that would make new blocks, the batches of transactions added to the network, arrive every 25 seconds instead of 75. The exchange now uses Zakura, a program that follows Zcash and checks its transaction history. Gemini [said Tuesday](https://www.gemini.com/blog/gemini-preps-for-faster-zcash-with-move-to-zakura) that Zakura caught up with the latest block in a little over six hours during its deployments.
